channel.title: Justin Valentine
channel.description: Robots and the tools around them, by Justin Valentine.

item.title: A test suite for the haptic wrist
item.description: I put all three joints of the final haptic wrist through bench tests for friction, inertia, bandwidth, large-signal tracking, Z-width and virtual walls, and compare it with the WHAM prototype.

item.title: Sisyphus, a bike trainer app for the Mac
item.description: My Mac app for running a smart trainer in ERG mode from a small overlay that floats over full-screen video.

item.title: A haptic lightsaber game
item.description: Sword fighting on a WAM with the haptic wrist. When the blades meet, the arm pushes back, harder near the hilt than near the tip. I go through how the force is computed, the opponents, the Meta Quest 3 viewer and Barrett’s booth at IROS 2026.

item.title: The Alberta wrist
item.description: The last haptic wrist in the series, which I design at Barrett Technology in 2026. It goes from a cardboard model in May, through printed prototypes, to machined parts for two wrists and a set of spares, and on to Barrett’s booth at IROS in September. I also go through the motor and ratio choices, the FEA and the measured results.

item.title: A Variable-Pitch Hopper
item.description: I'm building a one-legged hopper around a screw cam whose groove sets the gear ratio, plus the control board that runs it.

item.title: Teaching the Hopper Where to Put Its Foot
item.description: In simulation, I swap the hopper's tail for a corner-balanced wheel triad, place its foot with a measured one-hop return map, and soften its landings.

item.title: Getting this site off the ground
item.description: Why I keep this site as plain static pages.

item.title: Building the WHAM wrist
item.description: A two-joint, cable-driven haptic wrist for the WAM leader, with a thumb joystick for the follower’s last joint. It’s my biggest machining project so far, and it goes from a printed version in January 2026 to the WAM in April.

item.title: A direct-drive end-effector wrist
item.description: A 3D-printed leader wrist for the WAM with three directly driven joints and a bike-grip handle. The operator holds it like an end effector, with nothing strapped to the arm. I demo it at RISEx 2025.

item.title: The coaxial semi-differential wrist
item.description: A four-joint, cable-driven leader wrist for the WAM. Two of its drives are rings stacked around the forearm, and a fourth motor turns the whole wrist relative to the arm it’s mounted on.

item.title: Drawing sketches with guided flow matching
item.description: A course project where we generate sketches point by point with flow matching and classifier-free guidance, then have a Barrett WAM draw them on a whiteboard that presses back with a constant force.

item.title: Writing DECtalk songs with an RNN
item.description: My CMPUT 652 course project: a character-level LSTM, trained on 1,085 DECtalk song files, that writes new songs for the old speech synthesizer to sing.

item.title: HAL, a quadruped with an actuated spine
item.description: HAL is my quadruped, built like Solo 8 but with a motorized spine so it might do a backflip, or even a double. I go through the figure-skater math behind the spine and a year of building, then HAL Gym, where I'm training it to flip.

item.title: A simple direct-drive gimbal wrist
item.description: A gimbal wrist for the WAM, driven directly so it’s easy to prototype, that we use to test strapping the WAM to an operator’s forearm as an approximate exoskeleton.

item.title: A haptic mobile manipulator
item.description: A 7‑DOF WAM on a Clearpath Husky, driven from a second WAM so the operator feels what the robot touches. I design the mobile base and set up the sensors and ROS. We’re one of eight finalist teams in DND’s IDEaS challenge.

item.title: A spherical wrist after the Agile Eye
item.description: A three-motor spherical parallel mechanism I’m trying out as a haptic wrist, and why its Jacobian is the identity matrix at the home pose.

item.title: A 360° camera from six $20 action cameras
item.description: My CMPUT 428 final project with Justin Rozeboom: six cheap action cameras in a laser-cut hexagonal housing on an iRobot Create 2. We calibrate them and stitch their frames into cylindrical panoramas, then take a first try at structure from motion on the reprojected images.

item.title: Tiling the hyperbolic plane
item.description: My Python program for drawing regular hyperbolic tilings in the Poincaré disk. It reflects one polygon across its own edges over and over.

item.title: A painting robot
item.description: My CMPUT 312 final project with Yash Bhandari: a six-servo arm from AliExpress on a wooden stand that paints SVG files onto a slanted canvas with a brush.

item.title: Localizing a Create 2 with two lasers
item.description: My 2022 idea for finding a robot in a room from two laser ranges to markers on the walls. I work out the geometry in a pygame simulation and write Python to drive an iRobot Create 2 over its serial port.

item.title: Go on a sphere
item.description: Go on a board with no edges or corners. I start it in 2022 while taking a differential geometry course and finish it in 2026 as a playable game with a Monte Carlo tree search opponent.

item.title: A Rubik’s Cube solver
item.description: A Python program that simulates a cube of any size and solves the 3×3 with the beginner’s layer-by-layer method. I’ve also started a webcam scanner for it in OpenCV.
